summary: Opens a Bink video file (.bik). Copies the requested file name, normalizes it, and appends the .bik extension when missing; selects the Bink sound system (Miles for flag bit 1, DirectSound for flag bit 2) when a sound device is supplied, otherwise clears the sound track; builds the BinkOpen flag word from flag bits; opens the file directly and, on failure, retries through registered media directories. On success stores the Bink handle and the video width and height from BinkGetSummary and returns 0; otherwise reports the Bink error and returns -1.

operations.description: Copy the requested file name a2 into the local SrcStr buffer and normalize it via sub_589901.
If sub_587C20 reports that SrcStr does not already carry the extension stored at aBik, append the 4-byte extension text from aBik plus its trailing byte aBik[4] (byte_5DC0BC) at the end of SrcStr.

When flag bit 1 is set and the sound device a4 is non-null, register the Miles sound system via BinkSetSoundSystem(BinkOpenMiles, a4); on failure obtain the error text with BinkGetError, format the Miles-sound error message with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck, report it through sub_53C590 and return -1.

When flag bit 2 is set and the sound device a4 is non-null, register the DirectSound system via BinkSetSoundSystem(BinkOpenDirectSound, a4); on failure obtain the error text with BinkGetError, format the DirectSound error message with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck, report it through sub_53C590 and return -1.
When neither sound flag applies, clear the Bink sound track with BinkSetSoundTrack(0, 0) and seed the BinkOpen flag word with 0x4000.

Build the BinkOpen flag word from flag bits: with bit 0x10 set, add 0x60000000 plus 0x30000000 when bit 2 is set, with bit 3 adjusting the word via the 0x8FFFFFFF/0x9FFFFFFF masks to 0x20000000 or 0x50000000; without bit 0x10, add 0x30000000, 0x10000000 or 0x40000000 (mask-clearing 0x8FFFFFFF when combining 0x40000000).
Open the video directly with BinkOpen(SrcStr, flag word) and store the returned handle into the handle field this+0x0.

If the direct open failed, iterate the registered media directories: format the directory path with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck using the aSS_3 path format, walking the directory table at byte_8B5A3C in 132-byte steps, and call BinkOpen on each candidate path, updating this+0x0, until one succeeds or dword_8B8E30 directories have been tried.
On a successful open, call BinkGetSummary(handle, summary buffer) and copy the summary width into this+0x8 and the height into this+0xC.

Return 0 on success; if every open attempt failed, obtain the error text with BinkGetError, format the Bink-file error message with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck, report it through sub_53C590 and return -1.

clean_pseudocode: SrcStr = normalize(copy(a2)); if no extension from aBik: append it;
if (bit1 && a4) BinkSetSoundSystem(BinkOpenMiles, a4) else if (bit2 && a4) BinkSetSoundSystem(BinkOpenDirectSound, a4) else BinkSetSoundTrack(0, 0), flags |= 0x4000;
if (!h) for dir in directory table: h = BinkOpen("%s\\%s"(dir, SrcStr), flags);
if (h) { BinkGetSummary(h, summary); this.width = summary[0]; this.height = summary[1]; return 0; }
else { log("Error: %s for BINK file %s", BinkGetError()); return -1; }
